messages:
sam: Hi everyone, quick onboarding question. Trying to set up CI and i'm not sure whether to use a hosted key or sandbox key for our staging pipeline. Any strong opinions?
julie: for staging we usually recommend a sandbox key unless staging hits prod traffic or uses real customer data. sandbox = lower blast radius. :shield:
sam: got it. sandbox keys though sometimes hit rate limits quickly on parallel test runs?
ryan: yep, sandbox quotas are smaller by default. If you need higher concurrency for CI, ask devex for a temp bump or use a dedicated org service token with constrained scopes.
sam: can someone point me to the GH Actions pattern? i have something like:
```yaml
env:
  REDWOOD_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}
steps:
  - name: call api
    run: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Is that ok?
julie: that's fine, but prefer creating a repo-level secret for sandbox keys and a separate org-level service token for long-running runners. Also avoid hardcoding keys in workflows.
devex-bot: Tip: use short-lived sandbox keys for dev and long-lived service tokens for CI. See docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/dev-keys#ci-patterns
sam: what's the recommended name convention for secrets? we have a bunch: REDWOOD_KEY, REDWOOD_TOKEN, RW_API. Would rather standardize.
ryan: standard is REDWOOD_API_KEY for hosted and REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY for sandbox. Prefix with env like STAGING_ or CI_. Eg: STAGING_REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY. Makes audits easier.
security: also add key metadata in your repo README (who created it, purpose, least privilege). If it's a hosted key for production, ensure it is stored in KMS and not in plain GH secrets for high-risk repos.
sam: good call. Any advice on retries/backoff for 429s in CI tests? we see intermittent 429s in parallel test suites.
julie: a few options: reduce parallelism, add jittered exponential backoff on 429, or request quota increase for the sandbox token from devex if it's test-only. For CI you can also run a small local cache/mocking layer for generation requests to avoid hitting API for every test.
ryan: we also have a lightweight replay fixture in infra that records a few typical responses. ping infra and they can hook you up.
infra: can confirm — if you send a note to #eng-infra with the repo and expected concurrency we can provision a temporary larger sandbox quota for the test window.
sam: who should i DM to get an org service token?
devex-bot: devex@redwood.ai handles service-token requests. Template request: project name, repo, intended use, required scopes, test window.
security: quick reminder: service tokens should have scoped permissions (generation-only if that's all you need) and rotate periodically. Use KMS where possible.
sam: thanks! I'll open a ticket with infra for quota and follow devex template for the token. Appreciate the quick help :pray:
